title: Frontier Development — Pragmatic Clean Code and SOLID Convention

content.purpose: Guide future coding for the Frontier executable best-guess business-systems demonstration without overriding mission, architecture decisions, or completed functionality.
content.mission_guardrail: Land the Frontier Business Application Developer position through a credible, executable best-guess representation of Frontier business systems; demonstrate practical engineering rather than claim knowledge of Frontier internals.
content.guiding_principle: Optimize for understandable intent, changeability, and practical delivery. Perfect is the enemy of the good.

clean_code: Focused methods and classes with coherent responsibilities
Explicit control flow where it improves traceability
Encapsulation of invariants and deliberate state changes

solid.S: Single Responsibility — focused reason to change
solid.O: Open/Closed — extend at meaningful variation points; do not create speculative frameworks
solid.L: Liskov Substitution — substitutable implementations honor contracts
solid.I: Interface Segregation — narrow interfaces for actual consumers
solid.D: Dependency Inversion — abstractions at justified boundaries, not one per class

principles.dry: Consolidate meaningful duplication when it improves clarity; avoid premature generalization.
principles.kiss: Choose the simplest design that makes the current business behavior correct, explicit, and testable.
principles.yagni: Do not build anticipated infrastructure, models, or abstractions without current demonstrated need.

csharp_preferences: Prefer explicit business intent and named intermediate operations over densely compressed expressions.
Use records for data transfer/results when appropriate; use encapsulated services for behavior and invariants.
Use interfaces, DI, repositories, and adapters when there is a real substitution, testing, or infrastructure boundary.
Keep business rules distinct from persistence, external integrations, and presentation.
Use modern C# features when they enhance readability; avoid cleverness for its own sake.
existing_code_policy: Preserve verified functionality and previously passed tests.
No bulk refactoring or style-only rewrite.
Refactor locally when it produces concrete readability, safety, or maintainability value; reverify behavior.
Do not reopen completed stages merely to conform code style.
delivery_discipline: Implement incrementally toward mission value; preserve chronological business-flow development as the current working approach, not a newly invented global governance rule.
Use established Downloads ZIP plus PowerShell installer workflow; include Unblock-File and safe backup/install semantics.
Keep synthetic/demo assumptions clearly separated from known Frontier facts.
content.precedence: Project-scoped coding guidance; subordinate to human direction, operative SB governance and technical decisions, and current mission priorities. Does not change stage scope, project status, architecture, or system facts.
out_of_scope: No mandatory rewrite of Stage 1 or Stage 2 components.
No automatic migration of console harnesses to xUnit.
No new system architecture approval or decision on real ERP/WMS interfaces.
No edits to the general Development ReferenceShelf.
